set.body:
Problem:
SlurmSite.local hardwires SlurmLocal.default and Managed.durable, so the public Site SPI is backend-neutral while the implementation constructor is not reusable with another scheduler transport such as the existing SSH agent path.

Scope:
- Add one low-level resource-safe Slurm site constructor that accepts the managed batch executor, worker launcher or staging capability, verified result sink, store, and site configuration it actually requires.
- Express local CLI and SSH entry points as derived convenience constructors over that capability constructor.
- Keep low-level algebras available for advanced composition while retaining the five-line Sojourn facade.
- Isolate any unavoidable IO-shaped worker boundary rather than advertising false effect polymorphism.

Acceptance criteria:
- The base Slurm site constructor does not instantiate SlurmLocal, an SSH client, or a ManagedController internally.
- Sojourn.local, Sojourn.slurm local-CLI, and a clearly named SSH constructor are derived Resource-safe facades over shared assembly code.
- Local CLI and SSH use the same Site, TaskRunner, TaskHandle, outcome mapping, result attachment, and store semantics; only transport/interpreter capabilities differ.
- Construction and release ordering are tested so new submissions stop before dependent resources finalize and every admitted handle settles honestly.
- SSH disconnect after scheduler acceptance does not cancel the job; reconnect/reopen can recover the durable handle and result.
- Capability, protocol, authentication, staging, and scheduler failures remain distinct typed acquisition or task evidence.
- Compile-checked examples cover advanced injected construction plus five-line local CLI and SSH usage.
- The local fake/agent transport and local CLI interpreter pass one differential Sojourn batch conformance suite.
- Store, Batch, Pool, and Parity TCK laws stay green for the local backend, and Slurm Store/Batch laws pass on the disposable or configured controller.
- The existing S3 Slurm acceptance item is closed with execution evidence or linked to a single explicit external blocker before this item closes.
- Final architecture docs show capability ownership and confirm that adding a future REST interpreter requires a constructor adapter, not changes to Site or task semantics.
set.title: SCOMP.5: Derive local CLI and SSH sites from capability constructors
